Note::RegexAccessor::replace¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::RegexAccessor::replace(std::string_view pattern,
                                std::string_view replacement,
                                std::int64_t flags = 0) const

Rewrite Regex Matches In Every Cell¶

replace(pattern, replacement) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every non-overlapping match of pattern in each cell replaced by replacement. It is the pattern-based counterpart of Note::replace: reach for it when the target is a shape (a run of digits, a date, a bracketed span) rather than a fixed string.

pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression. replacement is an ECMAScript replacement string, so it may reference capture groups with $1, $2, … (and $& for the whole match, $$ for a literal $). Replacement is global by default — there is no “first only” mode here; use Note::replace_first for a literal first-only rewrite, or anchor the pattern.

flags¶

flags is a bitmask of match options; flags <= 0 (the default) is plain case-sensitive ECMAScript.

Bit (value)

Effect

1 << 0 (1)

case-insensitive matching

1 << 1 (2)

multiline — ^ and $ also match at line breaks

Failure¶

An invalid pattern throws pluss::Error before any cell is processed. The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note; a cell with no match is copied through unchanged.

Example 1: Replace Every Match¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"a1b22c333", "none"}).regex().replace(R"(\d+)", "#"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a#b#c#", "none"]

Each digit run — regardless of length — becomes a single #.

Example 2: Capture-Group Back-References¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"2026-08-02"}).regex().replace(
    R"((\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}))", "$3/$2/$1");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["02/08/2026"]

$1/$2/$3 are the year, month, and day groups, reordered by repl.

Example 3: Case-Insensitive Matching¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"Hello HELLO hello"}).regex().replace("hello", "hi", 1))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["hi hi hi"]

With flags = 1 all three spellings match.

Example 4: The Same Pattern Without Flags¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Hello HELLO hello"}).regex().replace("hello", "hi"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Hello HELLO hi"]

Case-sensitive: only the exact lowercase hello is rewritten.

Example 5: An Invalid Pattern Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::make_note({"x"}).regex().replace("(", "y");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

regex().replace: The expression contained mismatched ( and ).
